roles.title: Roles and permissions
roles.hint: A role is a set of permissions; every account has one or more roles. “Everything” grants every permission, including those later versions will bring. Renaming a role updates the accounts using it.
roles.name: Role
roles.badName: Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores (32 at most).

auth.title: Sign-in
auth.config: People sign in with the accounts of this page, usually one shared per role (for example “prestiti” for the desk).
auth.database: People sign in with personal accounts.
auth.personal: To give a person an account of their own: "New account", with their role and the password to change at the first login.

dialog.usernameHint: Lowercase letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore (2 to 32).
dialog.badUsername: Use lowercase letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore (2 to 32).
dialog.passwordHint: The password is not saved: only its hash is written in the configuration. Whoever is signed in with this account will have to sign in again.
dialog.removeHint: The account leaves the configuration; what it did stays in the log under its name. It can be undone from the configuration history.
dialog.mustChange: To change at the first login
dialog.mustChangeHint: For a person's account: at the first login they choose their own password, which the administrator does not know. Untick it for a shared account.

backups.title: Backups
backups.createdDeleted: Backup created: {{name}} ({{deleted}} old {{deleted:plural; one:backup; other:backups;}} deleted)
backups.empty: No backups yet. The first one runs at the scheduled time, or press “Back up now”.

catchUp.hint: The scheduled backup was missed (computer off): BiblioViva made it at start.

offsite.title: Last off-site copy

offsite.never: The service is enabled but has not written any result yet.
offsite.stale: The off-site copy is older than two days: check the offsite service.

restore.title: Restore
restore.hint: Choose “Restore…” on a backup of the list, or upload a BiblioViva archive (a backup, “Export everything” or “Export configuration”, up to {{maxMb}} MB; a larger one is copied into the server's backups folder or restored with bun run backup:restore). Everything is checked first, then only the chosen parts are restored: the others stay as they are.
restore.images: Images to restore: {{photos}} {{photos:plural; one:photo; other:photos;}}, {{covers}} {{covers:plural; one:cover; other:covers;}}.
restore.gapsTitle: Some data would be left without what it refers to:
restore.gap: {{rows:plural; one:{{rows}} row of “{{part}}” refers; other:{{rows}} rows of “{{part}}” refer;}} to “{{needs}}” that would not be there: add “{{add}}” to the choice.
restore.schema: The backup is from another version of BiblioViva (tables {{tables}}): it cannot be restored here.
restore.confirmHint: The chosen data and configuration are replaced by those of the backup. The configuration can be taken back from the history; for the data, make a backup first when there is no recent one.
restore.notArchive: The file is not a BiblioViva archive.

contents.title: What the backup contains
contents.database: Database: a full copy at every run (listed below).
contents.images: Photos and covers: copied every night into the “uploads” folder of the backup ({{photos}} {{photos:plural; one:photo; other:photos;}}, {{covers}} {{covers:plural; one:cover; other:covers;}} right now).
contents.imagesPending: Photos and covers: the first copy happens at the next run ({{photos}} {{photos:plural; one:photo; other:photos;}}, {{covers}} {{covers:plural; one:cover; other:covers;}} to copy).
contents.config: The configuration (templates, images, settings) is not in the nightly backup: use “Export everything” to get it.

export.hint: One ZIP file with the database, photos, covers and the whole configuration (templates and images included), ready for “bun run backup:restore”.

parts.title: Backup or export of some parts
parts.hint: Choose what to include: the library's data, the settings of each section, the templates, the images… “Create backup” keeps it in the list below, “Download” downloads it to the computer.

demo.confirmDescription: The patrons, books, loans and photos of the demo will be deleted. The classes and the teachers group stay. Every operator will be signed out.

areas.title: Area style

steps.step1: In Configuration → Print templates choose “Duplicate” on a template (for example {{path}}) and give it a new name.
steps.step2: With “Edit” design it or change its code; images are uploaded on the same page.
steps.step3: Come back here and check the preview: an unknown field or a missing file is reported.
steps.step4: To use it for real, choose it in the Cards or Labels settings.

upload.hint: To be used once, when moving from Koha: one row per open loan with the patron's card and the copy's barcode, and the loan and due dates when there are any. Import patrons and catalogue first; the template, with the columns needed, is downloaded below.

without.dueOn: Without the due_on column the due date is computed as at the desk, with the loan rules and the calendar.

calibration.title: Calibrate two-sided printing
calibration.intro: To print the cards on both sides of the sheet the back must fall exactly behind the front. Every printer moves the back a little: this test measures how much, once.
calibration.current: How the sheet turns: {{flip}}. Shift of the backs in use: {{x}} mm across, {{y}} mm down.

steps.print: Print the calibration sheet with the button below.

window.long-edge: In the print window choose “Two-sided”, flipping on the long edge, scale 100 % and no margins.
window.short-edge: In the print window choose “Two-sided”, flipping on the short edge, scale 100 % and no margins.

steps.cut: On the side with the large “1”, cut carefully along the black line.
steps.read: Turn the card over: on side “2” look where the cut edge crosses the two rulers and read the two numbers (with their sign: + or −).
steps.save: Type the two numbers below and save: the shift of the backs is corrected.
steps.check: Print the sheet again to check: the cut edge should now cross both rulers on 0.

drawing.title: What to read
drawing.label: Side 2 after the cut: the cut edge crosses the rulers
drawing.hint: The cut edge crosses each ruler: the number there is the value to type. Each tick is a millimetre, the numbers come every five.

fields.hint: The number where the cut edge falls, with its sign; 0 if it falls on zero.

calibration.next: After saving, the backs will be shifted {{x}} mm across and {{y}} mm down.
calibration.saved: Calibration saved: backs shifted {{x}} mm across and {{y}} mm down.

sheet.title: BiblioViva · calibration of two-sided printing
sheet.cut: Cut along the black line, then turn the card over.
sheet.read: Read on the two rulers where the cut edge falls.
